disclaimer: CFP derived from proposal-grain Functional User Requirements is an approximate early measurement per COSMIC Part 2, not a code-verified count. Epics tagged Assumed/Unknown rest on assumptions and should be re-measured against built artifacts.
rulesPrimer:
I now have all the material needed. Composing the primer.

## COSMIC v5.0 Movement-Counting Primer — Salesforce Delivery Scope

**1. External-system round-trip** (functional process calls another piece of software and gets a response — federated SSO to IdP, outbound API call). Count **2 movements**: one **Exit** (the request leaving to the other software, a functional user across the boundary) + one **Entry** (the response received back). Never Read/Write — another piece of software is a functional user, so its interactions cross the boundary and are handled by Exit/Entry, not persistent-storage movements.
> Part 2 §3.4 (manuals-indexed/part-2-mm-guidelines-v5-0-sep-2024/03-the-mapping-phase.md#L198-L213): "Do not identify a Read when the FUR … specify any software or hardware functional user as the source of a data group … Interaction with other functional users is by definition across a boundary … which is handled by an Entry data movement." (and symmetrically for Exit at L207-L213)

**2. CRUD on a persistent object** (user-triggered process). Per object of interest: **Create** = Entry (receive data) + Write; **Read** = Entry (receive key/request) + Read + Exit (return data); **Update** = Entry + Read + Write; **Delete** = Entry + one Write (delete is a single Write). One movement of each type per object of interest per process (Rules 13-15).
> Part 1 §4.5 (manuals-indexed/part-1-mm-principles-definitions-rules-v5-0-aug-2021/04-mapping-phase.md#L134-L149): "RULE 18: A Read shall: a) retrieve a single data group from persistent storage… RULE 19: A Write shall: a) move data attributes from a single data group to persistent storage… RULE 20: … A requirement to delete a data group … shall be a single Write data movement."

**3. Confirmation and error messages to the user.** Count **one Exit** total per functional process, covering all error/confirmation message types from all causes. Extra: if the message carries data beyond confirming acceptance/error, that additional data group is a separate Exit. No Entry/Exit for errors surfaced by a Read/Write or by the OS.
> Part 2 §3.4 (manuals-indexed/part-2-mm-guidelines-v5-0-sep-2024/03-the-mapping-phase.md#L267-L272): "One Exit is identified to account for all types of error/confirmation messages issued by any one functional process … from all possible causes … If a message … provides data in addition to confirming … this additional data is identified as a separate data group moved by an Exit."

**4. Distinct vs. one functional process.** Two processes are DISTINCT when they respond to different **triggering events**, or when a different **functional user** initiates them. A triggering event cannot be sub-divided and has either happened or not.
> Part 2 §3.2 (manuals-indexed/part-2-mm-guidelines-v5-0-sep-2024/03-the-mapping-phase.md#L63-L71): "Identify the separate events … the 'triggering events' … Identify which functional user(s) … may respond to each triggering event … Identify the functional process started by each triggering Entry."

**5. Single triggering Entry.** Each functional process is initiated by exactly one Entry from a functional user detecting the triggering event; a single Entry is counted per process. All data movements needed for **all possible responses to that triggering Entry** belong to the same functional process.
> Part 1 §4.2 (manuals-indexed/part-1-mm-principles-definitions-rules-v5-0-aug-2021/04-mapping-phase.md#L14-L26): "be initiated by an Entry data movement from a functional user informing the functional process that it has detected a triggering event … 'the set of all data movements that is needed to meet its FUR for all the possible responses to its triggering Entry'." (RULE 13, single Entry: L95-L99)

**Caveat:** Every process is ≥2 movements (one Entry + at least one Exit or Write). "User-triggered" here assumes a human/UI functional user; a clock-tick or inbound integration is itself a triggering Entry.

dataGroups.name: Lost-pet case
dataGroups.description: The reported case: caller name/contact number, pet species/breed/description, last-seen location and date, plus the generated case reference and status.

dataGroups.name: Microchip record
dataGroups.description: Registered-pet microchip records held in the animal registry, matched against the reported pet.

dataGroups.name: Found-pet record
dataGroups.description: Records of pets reported found, matched against the lost-pet report.

dataGroups.name: SMS confirmation
dataGroups.description: Outbound SMS to the caller carrying the case reference as confirmation of the logged report.

dataGroups.name: Confirmation/error message
dataGroups.description: On-screen acknowledgment or error surfaced to the agent for the logging action.

dataMovements.name: Enter lost-pet report
dataMovements.note: Single triggering Entry: agent submits all data describing the lost-pet case (caller, pet, location/date, contact). One Entry per object of interest (RULE 13/17).

dataMovements.name: Read microchip records
dataMovements.note: System checks animal registry for matching microchip records. A Read retrieves a single data group; microchip records are a distinct object of interest (RULE 18).

dataMovements.name: Read found-pet records
dataMovements.note: System checks for matching found-pet records. Distinct object of interest from microchip records, so a separate Read (single data group per Read, RULE 18).

dataMovements.name: Display microchip matches
dataMovements.note: Potential microchip matches displayed to the agent. Exit sends a single data group across the boundary (RULE 21).

dataMovements.name: Display found-pet matches
dataMovements.note: Potential found-pet matches displayed to the agent. Distinct object of interest, so a separate Exit consistent with the two Reads.

dataMovements.name: Create lost-pet case
dataMovements.note: Case persisted to storage; queue routing is taken as owner assignment on the same case object, so one Write per object of interest (RULE 19). See gap CG-E01-04.

dataMovements.name: Send SMS confirmation with case reference
dataMovements.note: Confirmation SMS carries the case reference (data beyond acceptance confirmation), so it is a separate Exit data group. No documented delivery-receipt response, so no return Entry (see gap CG-E01-03).

dataMovements.name: Confirmation/error message to agent
dataMovements.note: One Exit accounts for all confirmation/error messages the process issues to the agent, from all causes (primer #3).

gaps.gapOrQuestion: The registry check is counted as two objects of interest (microchip records and found-pet records) yielding 2 Reads + 2 Exits. If the system treats 'registry matches' as a single combined result set (one object of interest), it collapses to 1 Read + 1 Exit.
gaps.impactOrNotes: Swing -2 CFP (8 -> 6).

gaps.gapOrQuestion: Counted as ONE functional process (single triggering event: agent logs report; registry check, case creation, SMS and routing are all responses). If the UI has the agent run the registry search as a separate agent-initiated event before creating the case, it splits into two functional processes with different triggering events (primer #4).
gaps.impactOrNotes: Structural: two processes (e.g. search process E+R+R+X+X+X plus create process E+W+X+X) rather than one; total CFP shifts (~10 vs 8) and the mandatory second triggering Entry/confirmation Exit are added.

gaps.gapOrQuestion: SMS confirmation counted as a single Exit. If sending goes to an SMS gateway (peer software) and the FUR require a synchronous delivery/acknowledgment response, it becomes an Exit+Entry round-trip (primer #1).
gaps.impactOrNotes: Swing +1 CFP (return Entry from the SMS gateway).

gaps.gapOrQuestion: Routing to the Animal Management queue is folded into the case Write as an owner-assignment attribute (same object of interest). If the queue is a distinct persistent object of interest that receives its own write, a separate Write is required.
gaps.impactOrNotes: Swing +1 CFP (additional Write for the queue object).

dataGroups.name: Tree Works Request
dataGroups.description: The lodged request: tree location (address or map pin), reason/hazard description, and derived priority; the object of interest created and stored by the process.

dataGroups.name: GIS Boundary Validation
dataGroups.description: Round-trip to the asset/GIS boundary service: the location key sent out and the council-land ownership determination returned.

dataGroups.name: Crew Notification
dataGroups.description: Work assignment dispatched to the Parks & Gardens crew, carrying the request details and priority so they can action the job.

dataGroups.name: Resident Acknowledgement
dataGroups.description: Acknowledgement email to the resident conveying request receipt plus the expected response time (data beyond a bare confirmation).

dataGroups.name: Confirmation/Error Message
dataGroups.description: The single message stream back to the submitting agent covering all success/validation-failure/error outcomes of the submission.

dataMovements.name: Submit tree request
dataMovements.note: Single triggering Entry: agent (functional user) submits the captured location + reason. All response movements belong to this one process.

dataMovements.name: Query GIS boundary service
dataMovements.note: External round-trip Exit: the asset/GIS boundary service is another piece of software (functional user across the boundary), so the request leaving is an Exit, not a Read.

dataMovements.name: Receive council-land determination
dataMovements.note: External round-trip Entry: the validation response from the GIS service crosses the boundary as an Entry (paired with the Exit above).

dataMovements.name: Create works request
dataMovements.note: Create on the object of interest = Entry (already counted) + Write. Priority assignment is internal data manipulation, not a separate movement.

dataMovements.name: Notify Parks & Gardens crew
dataMovements.note: Exit to another functional user (the crew) across the boundary; carries request data, distinct from the agent confirmation Exit.

dataMovements.name: Send resident acknowledgement email
dataMovements.note: Separate Exit: the message provides data (expected response time) beyond mere confirmation, and goes to a different functional user (the resident).

dataMovements.name: Confirmation/error to agent
dataMovements.note: One Exit accounts for all error/confirmation messages (e.g., success, or 'tree not on council land') returned to the submitting agent from all causes.

gaps.gapOrQuestion: Photos 'if emailed in' — are they a separate object of interest entered as their own data group (an additional Entry), or attributes/attachments of the Tree Works Request captured in the single submission Entry? Counted here as part of the request Entry.
gaps.impactOrNotes: Swing +1 CFP if photos are a distinct Entry data group.

gaps.gapOrQuestion: Is the 'asset/GIS boundary service' a peer software across the boundary (Exit + Entry round-trip, 2 CFP as counted), or an in-boundary persistently-stored GIS layer that would instead be a single Read (1 CFP)?
gaps.impactOrNotes: Swing -1 CFP if it is a local persistent Read rather than an external round-trip.

gaps.gapOrQuestion: Does the process return an explicit confirmation/error message to the submitting agent (assumed here per the one-Exit error rule), or is submission feedback surfaced only implicitly by the Write/OS with no dedicated Exit?
gaps.impactOrNotes: Swing -1 CFP if no agent-facing confirmation/error Exit exists.

dataGroups.name: Rate Account Lookup Query
dataGroups.description: The account identifier the agent supplies to locate the rate account — either the property number or the property address.

dataGroups.name: Rate Account Payment Status
dataGroups.description: The payment position returned for the account: current balance, last payment date and amount, any arrears, and the next instalment due date.

dataGroups.name: Error/Confirmation Message
dataGroups.description: The process outcome indication to the agent covering all error/confirmation causes, e.g. account not found or finance-system unavailable.

dataMovements.name: Agent submits account lookup
dataMovements.note: Single triggering Entry from the agent (human functional user) detecting the event 'check rates payment status'; carries property number or address. All responses to this trigger belong to one functional process.

dataMovements.name: Query finance system for account
dataMovements.note: External-system round-trip: the finance system is a separate software functional user, so the outbound request crosses the boundary as an Exit (not a Read).

dataMovements.name: Receive payment status from finance system
dataMovements.note: Response leg of the external round-trip: balance, last payment date/amount, arrears and next instalment due date received back from the finance system across the boundary as an Entry.

dataMovements.name: Display payment status to agent
dataMovements.note: Exit of the retrieved payment-status data group to the agent (human functional user) so it can be read back to the caller.

dataMovements.name: Error/confirmation message to agent
dataMovements.note: One Exit accounts for all error/confirmation message types from all causes (e.g. account not found, finance system unavailable). Distinct from the payment-status Exit, which carries data beyond confirmation.

gaps.gapOrQuestion: Is the account status obtained by an external round-trip to a separate finance system (Exit+Entry), or does Salesforce read it from a local/replicated store (Read)? Also unclear whether the property-number and address lookups hit the same interface or two different retrieval mechanisms.
gaps.impactOrNotes: If a local persistent store is read instead of a cross-boundary call, movements 2-3 (X+E, 2 CFP) would be replaced by a single Read (1 CFP), and the agent-input+display Exits remain. Swing: roughly -1 CFP (4 vs 5). Two distinct retrieval interfaces would not add a process (still one triggering event) but could alter data-group/movement identification.

caveats: Identity verification is out of scope for this epic — the description states it happens before the lookup and the epic depends_on E10, so no verification movements are counted here.

The finance system is assumed to be a separate software functional user (strongly implied by 'retrieves ... from the finance system'), making the retrieval a cross-boundary Exit+Entry rather than a persistent-storage Read.
No local Salesforce Create/Update/Delete is described; the process is read-only from the caller's perspective, so no Write movements are counted.
Lookup by property number OR address is treated as one triggering event with alternative inputs (one functional process), not two processes.

epics.epicName: Set Up a Rates Payment Plan
functionalUsers: Post/email delivery system (other software/device functional user)

artifact.name: E04 Set Up a Rates Payment Plan

dataGroups.name: Payment Plan Request
dataGroups.description: Proposed instalment amount, payment frequency, and the target rate-account reference captured by the agent from the resident.

dataGroups.name: Hardship Policy Limits
dataGroups.description: Council hardship policy parameters (e.g. min/max instalment, allowed frequencies, maximum plan duration) the proposed plan is validated against.

dataGroups.name: Rate Account
dataGroups.description: The resident's rates account holding the outstanding-arrears balance needed to compute the instalment schedule.

dataGroups.name: Payment Plan Arrangement
dataGroups.description: The accepted payment arrangement (calculated schedule of instalments and dates) recorded against the rate account.

dataGroups.name: Confirmation/Error Message
dataGroups.description: Acceptance confirmation or validation/error notification returned to the agent for all outcomes of the process.

dataGroups.name: Payment Plan Confirmation
dataGroups.description: The written confirmation document detailing the agreed instalment schedule, dispatched to the resident by post or email.

dataMovements.name: Submit payment plan request
dataMovements.note: Single triggering Entry: agent detects the resident's request and submits the proposed instalment amount/frequency; all responses belong to this one functional process (Rule 13, single Entry).

dataMovements.name: Read hardship policy limits
dataMovements.note: Validation against council hardship policy limits requires retrieving the policy limits data group from persistent storage (RULE 18). Assumes limits are stored, not hardcoded — see CG-E04-01.

dataMovements.name: Read outstanding rates balance
dataMovements.note: Calculating the instalment schedule requires the outstanding-arrears balance retrieved from the rate account in persistent storage (RULE 18). Calculation itself is manipulation, not a movement. See CG-E04-02.

dataMovements.name: Record payment plan arrangement
dataMovements.note: Recording the arrangement on the rate account writes the payment-plan data group to persistent storage; one Write per data group per process (RULE 19).

dataMovements.name: Return confirmation/error to agent
dataMovements.note: One Exit accounts for all confirmation/error messages to the agent from all causes (e.g. hardship-policy validation pass/fail) in this functional process.

dataMovements.name: Issue written payment plan confirmation
dataMovements.note: The written confirmation carries the instalment schedule (data beyond a plain accept/error confirmation) dispatched to the resident via the post/email delivery system, a functional user across the boundary — a separate Exit data group. No return response is expected, so it is a one-way Exit (not a round trip).

gaps.gapOrQuestion: Are the council hardship policy limits stored persistently (validated via a Read) or hardcoded configuration/constants embedded in logic? The epic says the plan is 'validated against council hardship policy limits' without stating their source.
gaps.impactOrNotes: If limits are hardcoded constants there is no persistent-storage Read: swing -1 CFP (5 instead of 6). Counted as a Read (RULE 18) under the assumption limits are stored data.

gaps.gapOrQuestion: Is the outstanding-arrears balance read from the rate account within this process, or is it already supplied by dependency E03 and carried in on the triggering Entry? The epic implies calculation needs the balance but does not state the retrieval.
gaps.impactOrNotes: If the balance is passed in via the Entry rather than read here: swing -1 CFP (5 instead of 6). Counted as a Read under the assumption E04 retrieves current balance to compute the schedule.

gaps.gapOrQuestion: Is the calculated instalment schedule also presented back to the agent on-screen (for review/acceptance) as a distinct data group, separate from the pass/fail confirmation and the mailed confirmation?
gaps.impactOrNotes: If the schedule is displayed to the agent as additional data beyond the confirmation message, that is a separate Exit: swing +1 CFP (7 instead of 6). Not counted, as the epic only specifies a written confirmation to the resident.

gaps.gapOrQuestion: Does 'records the arrangement on the rate account' involve updating the rate account status (e.g. flagging it 'on payment plan') as a second, distinct object of interest in addition to writing the arrangement record?
gaps.impactOrNotes: If the rate account itself is also updated as a distinct data group, that is a second Write: swing +1 CFP (7 instead of 6). Counted as a single Write to the Payment Plan Arrangement data group.

epics.epicName: Report a Pothole or Road Defect
functionalUsers: Agent (human user capturing the resident's report via UI)
Roads team (recipient of the assigned works order)

artifact.name: Report a Pothole or Road Defect

dataGroups.name: Defect Report
dataGroups.description: Inbound report attributes captured by the agent: geographic location, defect type (pothole / damaged footpath / road defect), and severity.

dataGroups.name: Road-Defect Works Order
dataGroups.description: Persistent works-order record for a road defect, including location, defect type/severity, and the owning team; read for duplicate detection and written on creation.

dataGroups.name: Caller-Case Link
dataGroups.description: Association record joining the reporting caller to an existing duplicate works order/case so the caller is tracked against it.

dataGroups.name: Case Tracking Reference
dataGroups.description: The case/works-order reference number returned so the caller can track progress (new reference when created, existing reference when linked).

dataGroups.name: Confirmation/Error Message
dataGroups.description: Consolidated acceptance/validation/error feedback issued to the agent for all possible outcomes of the report submission.

dataMovements.name: Submit defect report
dataMovements.note: Single triggering Entry from the agent (functional user) detecting the 'resident reports a defect' event; all responses to it belong to this one process.

dataMovements.name: Duplicate check on existing defects
dataMovements.note: Read of persistent works-order store to find an existing duplicate defect at the same location within a radius (CRUD Read of the object of interest).

dataMovements.name: Create new road-defect works order
dataMovements.note: No-duplicate branch: Write persisting the new works order with the Roads-team assignment as an owner attribute (one Write per object of interest per process).

dataMovements.name: Link caller to existing case
dataMovements.note: Duplicate branch: Write persisting the caller-to-existing-case association. Distinct data group from the new works order; both branches are responses to the same triggering Entry so both live in this process.

dataMovements.name: Return tracking reference to caller
dataMovements.note: The reference number is data beyond mere confirmation, so it is a separate Exit data group from the generic confirmation/error Exit (covers both new and linked cases).

dataMovements.name: Confirmation/error message
dataMovements.note: One Exit accounts for all error/confirmation message types from all causes (invalid location, submission accepted, etc.) for the process.

gaps.gapOrQuestion: The epic states the caller is linked to a case and sent a reference, but does not specify whether the caller's identity/contact details are captured as a separate data group entered by the agent, or are already in session context (e.g. from the call). If captured as a distinct data group it would add one Entry.
gaps.impactOrNotes: CFP swing: +1 (extra Entry for Caller Contact data group) if caller identity is separately captured. Modelled as already-in-context here (no extra Entry).

gaps.gapOrQuestion: 'Assigns it to the Roads team' is modelled as setting an owner attribute on the works-order Write. If assignment instead pushes a notification/work item to the Roads team (a separate software/human functional user across the boundary), that is an additional Exit.
gaps.impactOrNotes: CFP swing: +1 (Exit to Roads team functional user) if an assignment notification is issued. No notification is stated, so excluded from the base count.

gaps.gapOrQuestion: 'Links the caller to that case' is treated as a Write to a distinct Caller-Case Link junction data group. If linking is instead an in-place update to the existing Road-Defect Works Order object of interest, it collapses into the same data group as the create branch and would not add a distinct Write.
gaps.impactOrNotes: CFP swing: -1 (from 6 to 5) if the link is the same object of interest as the works order rather than a separate association data group.

artifact.name: E06 Book a Hard Rubbish Collection

dataGroups.name: Booking Request
dataGroups.description: Resident/agent-supplied collection address, item types with counts, and the preferred collection window that initiate the booking.

dataGroups.name: Collection Allowance
dataGroups.description: The resident's free hard-rubbish collection quota and how many have already been used in the current year.

dataGroups.name: Item Category Rules
dataGroups.description: Reference list of item categories the council accepts for hard-rubbish collection, used to validate the requested items.

dataGroups.name: Collection Date Allocation
dataGroups.description: The date-allocation exchange with the waste scheduling service: outbound availability query and the returned next-available collection date.

dataGroups.name: Hard Rubbish Booking
dataGroups.description: The persisted booking record capturing address, validated items, allocated date, and status.

dataGroups.name: Booking Confirmation
dataGroups.description: The SMS message sent to the resident carrying the confirmed collection date and booking reference.

dataGroups.name: Booking Result Message
dataGroups.description: On-screen confirmation/error feedback to the agent covering all outcomes (e.g. no free collections remaining, unaccepted items, success).

dataMovements.name: Submit booking request
dataMovements.note: Single triggering Entry from the agent detecting the booking event; one Entry per functional process (Primer Rule 5).

dataMovements.name: Read free-collection allowance
dataMovements.note: Retrieve the resident's remaining free collections for the year from persistent storage (Primer Rule 2, RULE 18).

dataMovements.name: Read accepted item categories
dataMovements.note: Retrieve accepted-category reference data to validate requested items; distinct object of interest from allowance, so a separate Read (Primer Rule 2, RULE 18).

dataMovements.name: Request collection date
dataMovements.note: Outbound request to the waste scheduling service (another piece of software, a functional user across the boundary) — Exit half of the round-trip (Primer Rule 1).

dataMovements.name: Receive allocated date
dataMovements.note: Response received back from the scheduling service — Entry half of the external round-trip (Primer Rule 1).

dataMovements.name: Write booking record
dataMovements.note: Persist the confirmed booking to storage (Primer Rule 2, RULE 19).

dataMovements.name: Send SMS confirmation
dataMovements.note: Confirmation message to the resident via the SMS gateway; carries booking date/reference (data beyond mere acceptance) and targets a different functional user than the agent, so a separate Exit (Primer Rule 3). Modeled as fire-and-forget (no delivery-status Entry) — see gap CG-E06-01.

dataMovements.name: Agent confirmation/error message
dataMovements.note: One Exit accounting for all confirmation/error message types to the agent from all causes (e.g. quota exhausted, unaccepted items, success) — Primer Rule 3.

gaps.gapOrQuestion: Does the SMS gateway return a delivery/acknowledgement status to the functional process, making the SMS an external round-trip (Exit + Entry), or is it fire-and-forget (Exit only)? Modeled here as fire-and-forget.
gaps.impactOrNotes: CFP swing +1 (adds one Entry for the delivery-status response) if the SMS is a round-trip per Primer Rule 1.

gaps.gapOrQuestion: The epic states confirmation is by SMS but does not state an on-screen agent-facing confirmation/error message. Is there a distinct agent-facing message (order 8) separate from the resident SMS?
gaps.impactOrNotes: CFP swing -1 if error/confirmation to the agent does not exist as a distinct Exit; included here because error paths (no free collections, unaccepted items) must be reported to the triggering agent (Primer Rule 3).

gaps.gapOrQuestion: Are 'remaining free collections' and 'accepted item categories' two distinct persistent objects of interest (two Reads), or is the allowance derived by counting existing bookings? Modeled as two distinct Reads.
gaps.impactOrNotes: CFP swing +/-1 depending on whether allowance and category-rule data are the same or distinct objects of interest, or derived rather than stored.

caveats: Single functional process assumed: one triggering event (agent submits booking) drives all responses (Primer Rules 4-5).
External round-trip to the waste scheduling service counted as Exit+Entry (Primer Rule 1).
SMS confirmation counted as one Exit to the resident and modeled fire-and-forget; a separate Exit covers all agent-facing confirmation/error messages (Primer Rule 3).
No source code available (proposal grain) — implementationType/isApiCall omitted; measurement rests on defensible assumptions, hence confidence Assumed.

epics.epicName: Lodge a Noise or Nuisance Complaint

artifact.name: E07 - Lodge a Noise or Nuisance Complaint

dataGroups.name: Complaint Case
dataGroups.description: The nuisance/regulatory case record: nature of complaint (noise, illegal dumping, other), offending address, dates/times of occurrence, anonymity preference, and assigned Local Laws / Environmental Health team.

dataGroups.name: Confirmation Message
dataGroups.description: The single confirmation/error message returned to the agent acknowledging the complaint was accepted and the case created (or reporting a failure).

dataGroups.name: Case Reference
dataGroups.description: The case reference identifier issued to the complainant so they can track the lodged complaint (suppressed when the complainant is anonymous).

dataMovements.name: Enter complaint details
dataMovements.note: Single triggering Entry: agent (functional user) detects the resident lodging a complaint and enters the complaint data group (nature, address, dates/times, anonymity flag). All responses to this Entry belong to one process.

dataMovements.name: Write regulatory case
dataMovements.note: Create pattern (Entry + Write): the regulatory case, including its routing/assignment to the Local Laws / Environmental Health team, is persisted as a single Write of one data group.

dataMovements.name: Confirmation / error message to agent
dataMovements.note: One Exit accounts for all confirmation/error messages issued by the process to the agent from all possible causes.

dataMovements.name: Case reference to complainant
dataMovements.note: The case reference is data beyond mere confirmation, delivered to a different functional user (the complainant) across the boundary, so it is a separate Exit. Conditional on non-anonymous complainant, but counted once as part of the possible responses.

gaps.gapOrQuestion: How is the case 'routed to the Local Laws / Environmental Health team'? If routing is an assignment field stored on the case, it is already covered by the Create Write (0 extra CFP). If it triggers a notification to a separate team/system functional user, that adds +1 Exit; if that other software returns a response (assignment ack) it is an external round-trip adding +1 Exit + 1 Entry.
gaps.impactOrNotes: CFP swing of +0 to +2 (process CFP 4 to 6). Assumed the in-system-assignment interpretation (0 extra).

gaps.gapOrQuestion: Is the offending address (or complainant identity) validated/looked up against a persistent reference (e.g. property/address register) during lodgement? The description does not state any retrieval, so no Read was counted.
gaps.impactOrNotes: If an address/reference lookup exists, add +1 Read (process CFP 4 to 5). Not counted to avoid inventing movements.

functionalUsers: Council agent (human user capturing the application via UI)
Resident (receives the digital permit and confirmation email)
Payment gateway (other software, functional user across the boundary)

artifact.name: E08 Apply for a Parking Permit

dataGroups.name: Permit Application
dataGroups.description: The application data captured by the agent: vehicle registration, residential address, and permit type.

dataGroups.name: Property Register
dataGroups.description: Persistent register of properties/addresses used to confirm the applicant resides at the stated address.

dataGroups.name: Permit Allowance
dataGroups.description: The maximum number of permits allowed for a given address or zone, compared against permits already issued.

dataGroups.name: Fee Schedule
dataGroups.description: Persistent tariff of permit fee rates by permit type used to calculate the amount payable.

dataGroups.name: Payment
dataGroups.description: The payment request/authorisation data exchanged with the external payment gateway.

dataGroups.name: Parking Permit
dataGroups.description: The residential parking permit object of interest: existing permits already issued to the address (read for the allowance check) and the newly issued digital permit that is persisted and delivered.

dataGroups.name: Confirmation Message
dataGroups.description: Acceptance confirmation plus all error/rejection notices (failed residency, allowance exceeded, payment declined) surfaced to the agent/resident.

dataMovements.name: Submit permit application
dataMovements.note: Single triggering Entry: agent submits vehicle registration, address and permit type; all responses to this triggering event belong to one functional process.

dataMovements.name: Verify residency in property register
dataMovements.note: Read of persistent property register to verify the applicant resides at the stated address (Rule 18). Treated as persistent storage; see CG-E08-01 if it is an external service.

dataMovements.name: Read permits already issued to address
dataMovements.note: Read of existing permit records for the address to count them for the allowance check (Rule 18). Same object of interest as the permit being issued.

dataMovements.name: Read permit allowance
dataMovements.note: Read of the allowance data group compared against the issued-permit count (Rule 18). Assumed persistent; see CG-E08-02.

dataMovements.name: Read fee schedule
dataMovements.note: Read of fee rates to calculate the permit fee (Rule 18); the calculation itself is data manipulation and is not a movement. Assumed persistent; see CG-E08-03.

dataMovements.name: Send payment request to gateway
dataMovements.note: External-system round-trip: payment gateway is another piece of software (functional user across the boundary); the request out is an Exit.

dataMovements.name: Receive payment result from gateway

dataMovements.name: Persist issued permit

dataMovements.name: Send confirmation / error message

artifact.name: E09 Update Contact Details on Account

dataGroups.name: Contact Details
dataGroups.description: The resident's contact information held on the council customer account — phone, email and postal address — as the object of interest being edited and persisted to the customer master.

dataGroups.name: Confirmation Message
dataGroups.description: System response to the agent/resident confirming the contact-detail change was saved, and covering all validation-error/failure notifications for this process.

dataMovements.name: Enter new contact details
dataMovements.note: Single triggering Entry: the agent submits the new phone/email/postal-address values, informing the process of the triggering event (resident's request to update). One Entry per process (Rule 5).

dataMovements.name: Read existing account record
dataMovements.note: CRUD Update pattern (Entry + Read + Write): the current version of the contact-details object of interest is retrieved from persistent storage before the new values overwrite it.

dataMovements.name: Save updated details to customer master
dataMovements.note: CRUD Update Write: the validated contact-details data group is moved to persistent storage (customer master). One Write of this object of interest per process.

dataMovements.name: Confirm change to resident/agent
dataMovements.note: One Exit accounts for all confirmation and error/validation messages from all causes in this functional process; the confirmation carries no data beyond acknowledgement, so it is a single Exit.

gaps.gapOrQuestion: The epic states 'the system validates the new details' but does not say how. If validation only checks the entered attributes intrinsically (format/mandatory), it adds no movement. If it reads an internal reference data group (e.g., a postcode/address reference table) it adds one Read (+1 CFP). If it calls an external address-validation/verification service, that is an external-system round-trip adding one Exit + one Entry (+2 CFP).
gaps.impactOrNotes: CFP swing 0 to +2. Measured base assumes intrinsic validation (no extra movement). Resolve by confirming whether validation touches a reference data store or an external service.

gaps.gapOrQuestion: Identity verification is referenced ('After identity verification the agent edits the record') but the epic has depends_on: E10, implying verification is measured under E10. This measurement excludes any verification data movements. Confirm identity verification is fully out of E09 scope.
gaps.impactOrNotes: If any verification step is in fact in E09 scope, additional movements (likely an Entry + Exit/Read) would be added; excluded here to avoid double-counting with E10.

dataGroups.name: Caller-Supplied Identity Answers
dataGroups.description: The knowledge-based verification answers the agent enters on behalf of the caller — e.g. name, property address, date of birth, or account reference.

dataGroups.name: Customer Master Record
dataGroups.description: Stored customer identity attributes retrieved to validate the supplied answers.

dataGroups.name: Verification Attempt Log
dataGroups.description: Audit record of a single verification attempt (outcome, timestamp) recorded against the customer record.

dataGroups.name: Verification Result
dataGroups.description: The verified / failed outcome returned to the agent so the call can proceed.

dataMovements.name: Submit verification answers
dataMovements.note: Single triggering Entry: the agent detects the triggering event (need to verify a caller) and submits the KBA answers, initiating the process.

dataMovements.name: Read customer master to check answers
dataMovements.note: CRUD-read: retrieve the stored customer identity attributes from persistent storage to compare against the supplied answers (Primer Rule 2, RULE 18).

dataMovements.name: Log verification attempt
dataMovements.note: Write to persistent storage: log the verification attempt against the customer record (Primer Rule 2, RULE 19).

dataMovements.name: Return verified/failed result to agent
dataMovements.note: Exit carrying the substantive verified/failed outcome data group to the agent (functional output). Per Primer Rule 3, this same single Exit also subsumes any error/confirmation messaging from all causes.

gaps.gapOrQuestion: Does the system present the knowledge-based verification questions (or their expected answers) to the agent, or does the agent ask them independently? The description says 'the agent asks' the questions, implying no software output, but a question-retrieval step could constitute either an additional Exit within this process or a separate query functional process.
gaps.impactOrNotes: If the system supplies questions via an agent request: +2 CFP as a separate functional process (Entry + Exit). If it only pushes questions as part of this process: +1 CFP (an extra Exit). Current count assumes the agent sources questions outside the software, so 0 added.

gaps.gapOrQuestion: Is there a distinct error/confirmation-message Exit (e.g. 'customer not found', 'system unavailable', input-validation errors) separate from the substantive verified/failed Verification Result Exit?

One functional process assumed, triggered by the agent submitting answers; question presentation is assumed to occur outside the software (see CG-E10-01).
Delete/Update semantics not applicable — the logging step is a Create (single Write of a new attempt record).

artifact.name: Look Up Council Asset by Location

dataMovements.name: Return asset details and responsible team
dataMovements.note: Exit delivering the resolved asset details and responsible team to the requesting functional user; distinct data group beyond a bare confirmation.

dataMovements.name: Error/confirmation message
dataMovements.note: One Exit accounts for all error/confirmation (including no-asset-found) messages from all causes for this process (Primer Rule 3).
